thread:
ryan_support: Heads-up — multiple customers hitting a sudden vectors/sec regression on /v1/embeddings after yesterday's runtime rollout. Tokens/sec for text gen is stable. Symptoms: GPU at ~98%, embedding vectors/sec falls by ~60%, batcher queue depth climbs and we see fallback to tiny batches. Repro notes and logs below.

alex_marsh: Which customers? sample request patterns?

ryan_support: Two customers (acme-inc, searchify) on dedicated pools. They run dense embeddings for mixed short+long inputs (avg tokens ~40, but some long docs ~800). Happened ~2026-03-15T18:03 UTC (deploy window).

maria_lin: Pasting trimmed runtime logs:

```
[2026-03-15T18:03:12Z] batcher: enqueued request id=aa12 size=16 tokens=40
[2026-03-15T18:03:12Z] batcher: enqueued request id=aa13 size=1 tokens=780
[2026-03-15T18:03:12Z] batcher: flush triggered reason=timeout batch_size=17
[2026-03-15T18:03:13Z] runtime: selected kernel=kvcache_v2
[2026-03-15T18:03:14Z] runtime: gpu_util=98% queue_depth=118 avg_batch=3
[2026-03-15T18:03:15Z] runtime: fallback to model_variant=embed-lite-v2 (quantized) reason=gpu_backpressure
```

jordan_sre: Observed same on infra side: GPU 0/1 pegged, a long tail of tiny batches (1-4) despite high queue depth. Looks like dynamic batching is under-aggregating when long token requests interleave with short ones.

leah_devex: Was there any config change to the batcher or max_batch_tokens in the rollout? I remember a change to prefer latency-bound flushes.

opsbot: deploy-bot: Finished rollout runtime/v2.3.1 at 2026-03-15T18:02:58Z (changeset: prioritize-latency-batcher).

alex_marsh: If the rollout prioritized latency (smaller flush windows), that could explain tiny batches and lower token amortization. But why GPU stays at 98% and vecs/sec drops? Maybe kernel choice when long sequences present causes per-token slowdown (kvcache_v2 slower for mixed sequence lengths).

jordan_sre: Quick triage commands we ran:

```
# look for batcher queue and pod metrics
kubectl exec -it batcher-0 -- /bin/sh -c "curl -s localhost:9000/metrics | grep batcher_queue_depth"
kubectl top pod runtime-0 --containers
nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory,utilization.gpu --format=csv -l 2
```

ryan_support: Customer repro steps (minimal):
1) Fire 2k concurrent requests over 60s with mix: 70% short (10-50 tokens), 30% long (600-900 tokens).
2) Target per-request body:
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "embed-pro-v1",
  "input": ["<doc text>"],
  "client_meta": {"test_run": "regression-20260315"}
}
```
3) Observe: batcher_queue_depth rises, avg_batch_size drops to ~3, GPU util stays high, vectors/sec drops ~50-70% vs pre-rollout baseline.

maria_lin: Also saw dimension sanity logs — some client libs were sending extra empty strings which caused batcher to allocate a 1536-dim vector vs expected 1024 for embed-pro-v1. Not sure if that triggers a code path change but worth noting.

leah_devex: Good catch on the dims. If mixed dims appear in same batch we may be forcing a fallback code path that is slower. Can we get the exact request payloads?

ryan_support: I have one sample saved, sending to eng-runtime via secure channel.

alex_marsh: Short-term mitigation ideas: 1) revert batcher flush tweak to pre-rollout window, 2) increase max_batch_tokens to allow larger aggregations, 3) enforce strict input-dim validation at ingress so mixed-dim batches are rejected.

jordan_sre: For immediate customer mitigation, we've turned on auto-fallback to dedicated low-latency pools for acme-inc and reduced concurrency. That restored vecs/sec to ~85% of baseline but increased cost.

ryan_support: Next steps: - Eng-runtime to triage kernel selection for mixed-length batches (priority). - Devex to push a temporary ingress validation patch. - Support to coordinate customer mitigations and offer credits.

leah_devex: I'll open a small revert PR for the batcher latency change (quick rollback flag).

jordan_sre: Paging eng-runtime oncall -> @alex_marsh @maria_lin please ack and take P1.

opsbot: incident-bot: Incident created INC-2026-03-15-vecs-saturation, severity=P1, owners=[eng-runtime, eng-sre, devex].

ryan_support: Adding repro script link: https://internal.redwood/dev/projects/vecs-regressions/loadtests/regress-20260315.sh (run with ENV TARGET_POOL and CONCURRENCY).

alex_marsh: Acked. I'll start by reproducing on scale staging, then bisect the batcher change. Will post findings here.

maria_lin: I'll capture full runtime traces and kernel traces from the affected pods and attach shortly.

ryan_support: Thanks — will keep customers updated. :thumbsup:
